title: [Week 1] Material Design shell, campus search, and Home dashboard
body:
## Summary

Build the mobile-first **Home** experience and shared Material Design navigation. A student should be able to find a campus building or stop, open the map, and understand the best available next action without interpreting raw transit data.

## Background

The starter in [`src/components/`](https://github.com/nandanpraveen/ArchRide/tree/main/src/components) provides a Material shell and five destinations. The agreed design lives in `DESIGN.md`. Coordinate the public data contract with task 2 and wire its verified locations into this screen before closing the task. Tasks 7 and 8 later supply personalized Home sections.

This is a **Week 1** task, from **2026-10-11 to 2026-10-18**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Use Material UI controls and shared tokens for Home, Map, Plan, Saved, and Profile. Add responsive route/stop detail, alerts, notifications, and active-trip entry points without adding competing navigation.
- [ ] Implement keyboard-accessible, debounced search across verified buildings, entrances, and stops. Show the result type and location; selecting a result opens details or pre-fills Plan.
- [ ] Offer optional location access with an explanation and manual building/stop origin fallback. Request permission only after a user action; do not store continuous location history.
- [ ] Show nearby stops and available departures, a next-trip recommendation when an origin and destination are known, favorite shortcuts, and the next-class slot. Wire favorites and classes to tasks 7 and 8 rather than inventing data.
- [ ] Display relevant alerts and shared freshness/provenance labels. No source data means a useful unavailable state, not example buses or fake countdowns.
- [ ] Finish loading, empty search, offline, stale data, denied-location, retry, and signed-out states. Home remains useful without an account.
- [ ] Make Home and the shared shell usable from 320 px through desktop, with 48 px primary touch targets, visible focus, accessible labels, adequate contrast, safe-area padding, and reduced motion.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the transit importer, trip algorithm, or saved-item storage; their owners provide the data contracts.
- University account integration or unsupported official UGA branding.

## What we'll test

- Search with spaces, capitalization, aliases, duplicate building names, no results, a long result name, and a rapidly changed query.
- Location allowed, denied, unavailable, timed out, and outside the supported campus area; manual origin still works.
- Guest Home, a returning user, no nearby stops, no active service, source outage, and delayed responses arriving out of order.
- All five destinations, browser Back/Forward, direct links, keyboard-only search and navigation, screen-reader labels, and 320 px layout.
- Favorites and the next-class entry appear once tasks 7 and 8 integrate; opening them uses current data.

## Resources

- [Material UI with Next.js](https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/nextjs/)
- [Material Design navigation](https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-bar/overview)
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
- [Geolocation API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Geolocation_API)

title: [Week 1] Verify UGA data access and build central transit ingestion
body:
## Summary

Connect **real UGA transit data** to Supabase through one centrally scheduled importer. Preserve source identity and timing so every screen can tell the difference between current, stale, and missing information.

## Background

UGA links its public bus tracker at routes.uga.edu, but that alone does not establish permission to reuse a private endpoint. Resolve data access at the start of this week. The starter has `feed_status`, `/api/health`, and checked-in Supabase migrations. Agree the route, stop, arrival, alert, and freshness contracts with tasks 1, 3, and 4.

This is a **Week 1** task, from **2026-10-11 to 2026-10-18**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] By October 12, document the authorized transit source, permitted use, endpoint/credential requirements, fields, update frequency, quotas, attribution, and evidence of access. Identify a real approved alternative if needed. Escalate blocked access immediately; fixture-only operation cannot satisfy the release gate.
- [ ] Create migrations and generated types for buildings/entrances, routes, direction/variant patterns, stops, ordered stop occurrences, operating schedules when available, latest vehicles, historical observations, arrivals, observed arrival events, walking-cache entries, alerts, and affected entities. Coordinate private tables with task 3.
- [ ] Preserve upstream IDs, route-pattern and stop-sequence identity, source timestamps, receipt timestamps, and agency timezone. A loop can visit one stop more than once.
- [ ] Implement a server-side Supabase Edge Function or equivalent trusted worker to fetch, validate, normalize, and upsert shared data centrally. Keep credentials server-only and public reads protected with explicit grants and RLS; guests cannot write transit data.
- [ ] Schedule ingestion within verified source and free-plan limits. Prevent overlapping runs, bound request timeouts/retries, use backoff on rate limits, and make replay idempotent.
- [ ] Keep the last valid snapshot through partial failures. Mark its freshness truthfully; missing vehicles alone never imply a cancelled route. Reject malformed coordinates, foreign IDs, and old updates that would overwrite newer state.
- [ ] Expose source-provided arrivals and supported service alerts without creating unsupported estimates. Publish typed read contracts and sanitized fixtures for teammates, clearly separate from production data.
- [ ] Set explicit configurable retention and scheduled cleanup for observations, arrival events, old predictions, and walking caches. Keep latest state separate from history and record safe job-health diagnostics.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Scraping protected endpoints or bypassing source access restrictions.
- Custom machine-learning predictions, or claiming source accuracy before evaluation.

## What we'll test

- A real authorized successful ingestion and a repeated identical run; no duplicate rows or repeated-stop collisions.
- HTTP 429, 500, timeout, malformed JSON, partial source responses, no buses, old/out-of-order timestamps, and recovery after an outage.
- Coordinates at zero, missing route/direction, unknown stop IDs, repeated loop stops, cross-midnight service, and explicit source cancellation versus absence.
- Multiple visitors share the same cached feed; upstream requests do not multiply per browser.
- Guest read access, denied browser writes, no secrets in responses/bundles/logs, bounded database growth, and retention preserving latest state.

## Resources

- [UGA Campus Transit](https://tps.uga.edu/transit/)
- [UGA official bus tracker](https://routes.uga.edu/)
- [Supabase Cron](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/cron)
- [Supabase Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions)
- [Supabase row-level security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)

title: [Week 1] Private database, authentication, profile, and preferences
body:
## Summary

Let students sign in and manage **private travel preferences** while keeping public transit browsing open to everyone. Protect every personal table with ownership rules and provide a complete sign-out and account-deletion flow.

## Background

The starter supplies browser/server Supabase clients, session-refresh proxy, and an owner-only `profiles` table. Expand that foundation in `supabase/migrations/` and [`src/lib/supabase/`](https://github.com/nandanpraveen/ArchRide/tree/main/src/lib/supabase). Coordinate table shapes with tasks 7–10 and the admin access model with task 11.

This is a **Week 1** task, from **2026-10-11 to 2026-10-18**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Finish email-based sign-up/sign-in, verification callback, resend, expired-link/error handling, session persistence/refresh, password recovery if passwords are chosen, and sign-out using Supabase Auth. Configure allowed redirects for local, preview, and production environments without open redirects.
- [ ] Extend profiles/preferences with display name, email display, default manual origin, walking pace, arrival/safety buffer, theme, notification types, quiet hours, and America/New_York schedule timezone. Validate bounded values on the server.
- [ ] Provide migrations and generated types for favorites, named saved trips, classes, active trip sessions, reminder jobs, notifications, and push subscriptions if supported. Use owner IDs, foreign keys, appropriate indexes, uniqueness, timestamps, and cascades.
- [ ] Enable RLS on every exposed table and explicit minimal grants. Test SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and attempted ownership reassignment. Public transit is readable by guests; private rows belong only to their user.
- [ ] Finish Profile UI, shared preference application, links to saved items/classes/notifications, and guest-to-sign-in entry points. The theme preference affects the complete shell and contrast is checked in each supported theme.
- [ ] Implement confirmed account deletion through an authenticated server-only operation: verify current identity, revoke/sign out sessions, remove owned records and subscriptions, and delete the Auth account. Treat still-valid access tokens as a deletion test case.
- [ ] Keep secret/service-role credentials outside browser code. Use validated server identity and trusted admin roles; never authorize from editable user_metadata.
- [ ] Document location/privacy behavior, personal-data retention, account deletion, and the student-built affiliation statement in the app.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- University SSO/course import, additional social providers, or storing a continuous location trail.
- Implementing the favorites, schedule, and reminder feature screens owned by later tasks.

## What we'll test

- Guest access to all public transit screens; private requests rejected when signed out.
- Sign-up, verified and expired links, invalid redirects, duplicate email, sign-in failure, refresh, multiple tabs, sign-out, and recovery.
- Two independent users cannot read or change each other’s records by guessing IDs; anonymous access and owner-ID changes fail.
- Invalid preference limits, saved defaults, theme persistence, keyboard forms, and quiet hours crossing midnight.
- Account deletion cancels jobs/subscriptions and removes personal rows; another user survives; old tokens cannot recreate or read private data.

## Resources

- [Supabase server-side Auth for Next.js](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/server-side/creating-a-client)
- [Supabase row-level security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
- [Managing user data and deletion](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data)
- [Supabase API keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/api-keys)

title: [Week 1] Live map, route directory, and boarding-stop details
body:
## Summary

Build the **Map**, route directory, route details, and stop details so students can identify the correct bus and boarding point. Use real source positions and label stale locations clearly.

## Background

Use task 2’s normalized public data and coordinate search/detail navigation with task 1. The starter Map page is intentionally empty. Choose a maintained map renderer and an authorized tile provider, document attribution and limits, and keep maps client-side where required by Next.js.

This is a **Week 1** task, from **2026-10-11 to 2026-10-18**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Render verified route paths, stops, and latest vehicles on a pannable mobile map. Keep consistent labeled route colors across filters, map, Home, and details.
- [ ] Add route filters, selected vehicle/stop detail panels, optional user-location recentering, and a list alternative for keyboard and screen-reader users. Do not demand location permission to browse.
- [ ] Build a searchable route directory with route direction/variant, ordered stop occurrences, available operating information, path, and affected alerts.
- [ ] Build stop details with boarding location, serving routes/directions, up to the next three valid arrivals when supplied, update time/provenance, and alerts. Never fabricate missing arrivals.
- [ ] Provide walking directions to the actual verified boarding point, using task 5’s walking contract or an explicit external directions link until that contract is integrated.
- [ ] Expose save-stop actions integrated by task 7 and links to Plan. Support direct URLs for route and stop details and sensible Back behavior.
- [ ] Style current versus stale vehicle positions distinctly, with text explanations, and stop refreshing when the page is hidden if that fits the shared polling design. Clean up subscriptions/listeners.
- [ ] Handle map loading/failure, offline, no route selected, no service, invalid detail IDs, no GPS, overlapping markers, route changes, and mobile panel/map gestures.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Custom tile hosting or a guessed route path reconstructed from unverified data.
- Transfers, private location tracking, or inferring route closures from missing buses.

## What we'll test

- A bus and a stop open the correct detail; route filtering preserves the right markers and colors.
- A loop repeats one physical stop, opposite directions share a stop name, and multiple vehicles overlap.
- Fresh, stale, absent, and malformed coordinates; old positions never appear as live.
- One/two/three arrivals, no predictions, a cancelled source prediction, unknown route IDs, and service after midnight.
- Direct URLs, browser Back, keyboard/list fallback, narrow touch panels, attribution visibility, failed tiles, and cleanup after navigation.

## Resources

- [Material UI with Next.js](https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/nextjs/)
- [MapLibre GL JS documentation](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/)
- [UGA official bus tracker](https://routes.uga.edu/)
- [OpenStreetMap tile policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/)

title: [Week 2] Building-to-building planner and bus-versus-walking comparison
body:
## Summary

Let a student choose an origin and destination and compare **walking directly** with a **complete single-bus journey**. Recommend only buses they can actually reach before boarding.

## Background

This uses task 2’s route patterns/stop occurrences, task 4’s boarding locations, and task 3’s walking/buffer preferences. Put the calculation behind a typed, testable planning module and expose it through Next.js server code. Agree estimate/freshness interfaces with task 6 before implementing ranking.

This is a **Week 2** task, from **2026-10-18 to 2026-10-25**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Accept current location, building/entrance, stop, or selected map point as origin; search verified buildings/stops for a destination. Preserve usable manual inputs when GPS is denied.
- [ ] Choose and verify an authorized walking-routing provider or campus pedestrian graph. Use actual pedestrian paths and known entrances, preserve attribution, cache by locations/preferences with expiry, and document limits. A straight-line distance cannot be labeled a verified walk.
- [ ] Generate direct single-bus candidates using the ordered route pattern, correct direction, and distinct stop occurrences. Include walking to board, waiting after arrival at the stop, riding, and walking from the exit to the destination.
- [ ] Exclude buses whose boarding time is earlier than the user’s estimated stop arrival plus the safety buffer. Rank supported candidates against direct walking using total travel time and the chosen walking preference.
- [ ] Show complete journey steps, route/direction, boarding and exit stops, total duration, destination arrival, amount of walking, estimate provenance, and a plain-language recommendation.
- [ ] Implement leave-now planning and a typed arrival-deadline input consumed by task 6. Recalculate when the query, preference, or current data changes; never reuse expired bus selections.
- [ ] Expose unsupported journeys, missing walking paths, insufficient/stale arrivals, no active service, and outside-campus inputs honestly, with a valid walk-only option where available.
- [ ] Wire Plan into Home search, route/stop details, and saved-trip/class entry points. Use accessible Material origin/destination fields and results.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Multi-bus transfers, off-campus general transit planning, or unverified accessible-route claims.
- Invented pedestrian shortcuts through buildings or closed areas.

## What we'll test

- Every displayed total equals the walk + wait + ride + final walk; waiting starts after the student reaches the stop.
- A bus just reachable, exactly at the safety threshold, already departed, and unreachable even though its displayed ETA is short.
- Identical origin/destination, one-way loops, repeated stops, opposite direction, route variants, no direct bus, and campus boundaries.
- Walking faster, bus faster, equal-time ties, preferred less walking, missing entrance, path-provider outage, and cache expiry.
- Reversed inputs, rapid edits/out-of-order responses, midnight service, denied GPS, and saved-trip recalculation with different live vehicles.

## Resources

- [Next.js App Router](https://nextjs.org/docs/app)
- [Next.js Route Handlers](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers)
- [OpenStreetMap routing resources](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Routing)
- [Playwright assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions)

title: [Week 2] Arrival estimates, deadline assessment, and reliability evaluation
body:
## Summary

Make every arrival estimate honest and let students set an **arrive-by deadline**. Show whether a trip looks on time, tight, late, or too uncertain to assess, using evidence rather than unsupported confidence labels.

## Background

Task 2 supplies source estimates and observations; task 5 supplies complete journey candidates. Source ETAs are the initial baseline. This task owns estimate interpretation, arrive-by planning, and evaluation, not a second independent trip planner. Agree semantics with tasks 1, 4, 9, and 10.

This is a **Week 2** task, from **2026-10-18 to 2026-10-25**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Create one shared arrival representation with source/calculated provenance, source time, received time, validity, and explicit missing/stale reasons. All arrival surfaces use it.
- [ ] Display absolute/local arrival time, a last-updated label, and a countdown only while valid. Define documented freshness thresholds from verified source cadence; use a controllable clock in tests.
- [ ] Implement arrive-by searches over supported departure/service data, including walking and buffers. Do not apply a current live ETA to a future time outside its valid horizon; explain unsupported future planning.
- [ ] Assess full destination arrival against the deadline and user buffer as on time, tight timing, likely late, or insufficient data. Explain the deciding factor and label all outcomes estimates.
- [ ] Collect matched prediction/observed-arrival evaluation records with route pattern and stop occurrence, deduplication, timestamps, and retention. Distinguish an observed stop arrival from a guessed proximity event.
- [ ] Produce a reproducible evaluation report with sample counts, error distribution, bias, stale/missing rate, and source coverage. Split by route/time only where sample sizes support it.
- [ ] Enable arrival windows or custom adjustments only when evaluation supports their calibration. Otherwise ship the source baseline with uncertainty text; no invented high/medium/low confidence scores.
- [ ] Update Home, route/stop details, planner, and active-trip/reminder contracts so stale or absent estimates cannot silently become zero-minute arrivals.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Training a machine-learning predictor, promising perfect arrivals, or making claims from fixture-only evaluation.
- Using live estimates as future scheduled departure times without source support.

## What we'll test

- A deadline exactly met, buffer boundary, tight/late classification, a past deadline, invalid input, and insufficient data.
- Before/after midnight, America/New_York daylight-saving changes including November 1, and different client timezones.
- Future requested trips with and without supported operating schedules; no current bus reused hours into the future.
- An estimate expires while a page stays open, an update moves backwards, negative time, source cancellation, and disconnected feeds.
- Repeated stop visits matched to the correct prediction, tiny evaluation samples, missing observations, and uncensored failure counts.

## Resources

- [GTFS Realtime trip-update semantics](https://gtfs.org/documentation/realtime/reference/)
- [MDN Intl.DateTimeFormat](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DateTimeFormat)
- [UGA official bus tracker](https://routes.uga.edu/)
- [Playwright assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions)

title: [Week 2] Guest favorites and synced named saved trips
body:
## Summary

Let students save **favorite stops** and **named journeys**, manage them on Saved, and reuse them from Home. Opening a saved journey must plan against current information instead of replaying an old bus choice.

## Background

Use task 3’s private tables and Auth, task 4’s stop details, and task 5’s planner. Guests use local storage; signed-in users sync through Supabase. Integrate the favorite and saved-trip slots left by task 1 before closing this task.

This is a **Week 2** task, from **2026-10-18 to 2026-10-25**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Add save/unsave actions to stop details and trip results. Save journey origins/destinations and preferences, not an expiring vehicle or prediction.
- [ ] Build the Saved page with stop favorites, named journeys, rename, reorder, remove with useful feedback/undo, and links to the correct stop or fresh Plan result.
- [ ] Support guests with versioned local data and signed-in users with owner-only Supabase rows. Explain that guest items stay on the current device.
- [ ] On sign-in offer a clear merge/import of guest items, deduplicate equivalent stops/journeys, retain valid names/order, and avoid silently overwriting cloud items.
- [ ] Handle optimistic updates, server rejection, retries, concurrent tabs/devices, signed-out state, and network loss without losing a successful change.
- [ ] Populate Home favorites/recent saved-journey actions and reflect rename/reorder/removal across the app.
- [ ] Handle retired stops/buildings, changed route patterns, and corrupted/old local records. Mark invalid saved items and let the student repair or remove them.
- [ ] Keep personal items off shared caches and out of another user’s session after account switching or deletion.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Saving historical live bus choices or sharing a student’s private journey list publicly.
- A second authentication system or a custom synchronization backend.

## What we'll test

- Guest refresh, blocked/full local storage, corrupted JSON, schema upgrade, duplicate save, and empty Saved.
- Rename to blank or a long value, reorder by keyboard, remove/undo, and undo after the server rejects an update.
- Two devices update the same item, offline retry, sign-out/sign-in to a different account, and two-user RLS attacks.
- Guest/cloud merge with duplicate journeys, differently named journeys, cancelled merge, and invalid source IDs.
- A saved journey opened later uses current arrivals; expired/deleted routes do not produce a stale recommended bus.

## Resources

- [Supabase row-level security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
- [Supabase JavaScript upsert](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/upsert)
- [Web Storage API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Storage_API)
- [Material UI with Next.js](https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/nextjs/)

title: [Week 2] Weekly class schedule and next-class travel planning
body:
## Summary

Let students manually enter a **weekly class schedule** and use it to plan their next campus trip. Surface the next class on Home and calculate when to depart when an origin and enough transit data are available.

## Background

Task 3 owns private class tables and preferences; task 5 plans journeys; task 6 assesses time and data validity. Task 10 delivers reminders. Campus class times use America/New_York regardless of the phone’s current timezone.

This is a **Week 2** task, from **2026-10-18 to 2026-10-25**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Build a Material schedule editor and weekly list for class label, verified building/entrance, weekday(s), local start time, arrival buffer, enabled state, and reminder toggle per class.
- [ ] Allow create, edit, duplicate if useful, and delete with confirmation/undo. Validate missing destinations, bounded buffers, valid local times, and repeated weekday values.
- [ ] Compute the next occurrence in America/New_York, preserving wall-clock class time across daylight saving changes. Specify behavior for simultaneous classes, overlapping entries, and classes already started.
- [ ] Show the next enabled class/destination on Home with a Plan action. Use a known manual/default/GPS origin without silently assuming the user is at their last class.
- [ ] Calculate a suggested leave time from the complete supported journey and class arrival buffer. If future transit predictions are unsupported, expose the limitation and a supported walk estimate rather than inventing future bus timing.
- [ ] Sync signed-in schedules privately through Supabase; give guests a clear sign-in path for schedule synchronization. Never fetch private university course information.
- [ ] Expose a timezone-aware next-occurrence and reminder-job contract for task 10. Editing/removing/disabling a class invalidates obsolete reminder jobs.
- [ ] Link classes from Profile and cover empty, save failure, unavailable building, invalidated destination, and network-loss states.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- University login, course scraping/import, academic calendar inference, or claiming knowledge of cancellations/holidays.
- Background reminders themselves; task 10 owns delivery.

## What we'll test

- One class, multiple weekdays, weekend classes, same-time classes, overlapping classes, disabled classes, and no future class this week.
- Sunday-to-Monday rollover, midnight, before/after class start, buffer larger than available time, and November 1 daylight-saving transition.
- A phone in a different timezone still shows the correct campus schedule time.
- Editing time/building or deleting a class updates Home and cancels its old reminder; a retired building is recoverable.
- Unknown origin, denied GPS, unsupported future bus predictions, offline save retry, and cross-user privacy.

## Resources

- [MDN Intl.DateTimeFormat](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DateTimeFormat)
- [Temporal documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Temporal)
- [Supabase row-level security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
- [Material UI with Next.js](https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/nextjs/)

title: [Week 3] Active trips, relevant service alerts, and missed-bus recovery
body:
## Summary

Guide a student through an **active journey** and help them recover when the bus is missed or the plan changes. Show relevant service alerts at the point where they affect the trip.

## Background

This connects task 2’s alerts, task 4’s route/stop details, and tasks 5–6’s planning and estimates. An active session records the chosen journey and student-confirmed progress, not a continuous private location trail. Task 11 supplies labeled manual notices.

This is a **Week 3** task, from **2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Let the student start, resume, and end a trip with walk-to-stop, wait/board, ride, exit, and final-walk steps. Show the route direction, boarding and exit stops, timing, freshness, and destination.
- [ ] Persist an owner-only signed-in active session and a limited local guest session with expiry. Reopening the app revalidates the trip against current data.
- [ ] Aggregate active agency alerts and separately labeled manual notices. Filter by affected route/stop/time, expose details and validity, and integrate alerts into Home, map details, Plan, and active trips.
- [ ] When an estimate changes materially, a valid source cancellation occurs, or a user confirms a missed bus, recalculate feasible alternatives: next bus, another boarding stop, another supported direct route, or walking.
- [ ] Explain the tradeoff and revised deadline assessment. Require a student confirmation when a missed bus or boarding cannot be determined reliably; a disappearing vehicle is not a closed route.
- [ ] Avoid repeated recovery prompts and preserve the original destination and preferences. Dismissed/expired alerts stop affecting the current recommendation appropriately.
- [ ] Provide explicit arrived, end/cancel, stale/no-data, reroute unavailable, offline, and destination-changed states. Wire trip events into task 10’s notification/reminder contract.
- [ ] Use accessible Material detail panels, clear progress text, keyboard actions, and a safe exit from every stage.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Multi-bus transfers, automatic boarding claims from weak GPS, or route-closure inference from missing vehicles.
- Continuous user location storage or unsupported agency notices.

## What we'll test

- Start/resume/end as guest and user; refresh mid-trip, completed-trip expiry, sign-out, and account switching.
- Bus missed, student still boarding, bus temporarily missing, explicit cancellation, detour, alert expiry, and multiple affected routes.
- Every offered recovery is reachable and direction-correct; none uses an already departed bus.
- A faster walk, next bus, alternate stop, no alternative, stale feed, and deadline status changing after recovery.
- Duplicated/reordered updates, dismissed notices, clock changes, keyboard trip controls, and labelled agency versus manual alerts.

## Resources

- [GTFS Realtime service-alert semantics](https://gtfs.org/documentation/realtime/reference/)
- [Supabase row-level security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
- [Material UI with Next.js](https://mui.com/material-ui/integrations/nextjs/)
- [Playwright assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions)

title: [Week 3] Leave-now reminders and notification center
body:
## Summary

Build **in-app leave-now reminders** and a notification center for trips, classes, and relevant service alerts. Background web push is included only for verified supported browsers/devices and must never be promised when delivery is unavailable.

## Background

Task 8 supplies recurring classes, task 9 supplies active-trip events, and tasks 5–6 supply walking time and valid estimates. Reuse task 3’s private reminder/notification tables and preferences. Clarify the in-app-only experience before implementing optional push.

This is a **Week 3** task, from **2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Compute leave-now time from boarding time minus walk-to-stop and the configurable safety buffer, or from a valid walk-to-class plan. Recompute when source changes affect feasibility.
- [ ] Deliver in-app reminders while the app is active, with notification center history, read/unread, clear/expiry behavior, timestamps, links to the affected trip/class/alert, and a useful empty state.
- [ ] Support per-class toggles, per-type preferences, quiet hours crossing midnight, timezone-aware timing, and account-wide notification settings in Profile.
- [ ] Schedule trusted server jobs only where needed using Supabase Cron/Edge Functions and owner-only data. Use a deterministic deduplication key, retries with bounds, cancellation, expiry, and clock-controlled tests.
- [ ] Cancel or replace obsolete jobs after class edits/deletion, trip end/reroute, preference changes, sign-out where appropriate, and account deletion. Never send expired leave-now prompts.
- [ ] Assess and document the browser/device support matrix for web push, including iOS installation requirements. If supported targets are chosen, implement HTTPS/service worker, explicit opt-in, subscription storage, server-only push keys, revocation, and failure cleanup.
- [ ] On unsupported devices or denied permission, provide an honest in-app-only explanation. Do not request notification permission on first page load or claim reminders work after the app closes without a verified push path.
- [ ] Keep lock-screen content minimal and private; cross-user subscriptions and notifications must be inaccessible. Integrate Home and active-trip notification entry points.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Native mobile apps, SMS/email reminder services, or guaranteed OS-level notification delivery.
- Background push on browsers/devices that cannot support the verified implementation.

## What we'll test

- A reachable bus, a changed ETA, a missed bus, walking-only class reminder, and stale/missing ETA without a made-up leave time.
- Exact reminder boundary, late job, duplicate/retried job, browser sleep/resume, clock skew, and expired notifications.
- Quiet hours across midnight, timezone differences and daylight saving, per-class disabled state, and preference changes after scheduling.
- Class deletion, trip cancellation, account deletion, sign-out/account switch, invalidated push subscription, and two-user access tests.
- Permission allowed/denied/revoked, unsupported browser, offline, installed versus uninstalled iOS web app, and in-app fallback.

## Resources

- [Supabase Cron](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/cron)
- [Web Push API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Push_API)
- [Notifications API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notifications_API)
- [WebKit web push support](https://webkit.org/blog/13878/web-push-for-web-apps-on-ios-and-ipados/)

title: [Week 3] Restricted admin tools, maintenance, and data-quality operations
body:
## Summary

Give trusted maintainers a small **restricted admin screen** for feed health, failed jobs, data corrections, manual notices, and prediction evaluation. Make routine maintenance safe enough for the team to operate after launch.

## Background

Tasks 2, 6, and 10 create the importer, evaluation records, and reminder jobs. Task 3 owns identity and trusted admin authorization. Prefer a focused `/admin` surface and existing Supabase operations over a new generalized admin platform.

This is a **Week 3** task, from **2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Protect admin pages and every backing server operation with server-validated identity and a trusted admin role stored outside editable user metadata. Non-admin authenticated users and guests have no admin access.
- [ ] Show last attempted/successful ingestion, feed freshness, safe error summaries, failed/retried jobs, source rate-limit state, and current retention/storage usage. Do not expose secrets or private student travel data.
- [ ] Offer bounded, audited retry controls that respect importer/job concurrency and upstream quotas. A repeated click must not create duplicate workers or reminder delivery.
- [ ] Support verified building/entrance corrections with validation and audit fields. Keep manual overrides separate from imported source values so the next import does not silently erase them.
- [ ] Create/edit/expire clearly labeled manual notices with affected routes/stops, valid-from/until, author, and provenance. Never display them as agency notices.
- [ ] Expose task 6’s evaluation report with sample counts and limits; unmeasured prediction quality remains explicitly unmeasured.
- [ ] Implement and verify scheduled retention cleanup, failed-job handling, revoked subscription cleanup, and useful indexes/query plans. Document backup/export and restoration options available on the actual plan.
- [ ] Write an operations runbook covering source outage, stale feed, quota exhaustion, lost worker credentials, data correction, rollback, restore, and account deletion. Add logs/alerts that avoid personal data.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- Broad access to personal schedules/location data, a public admin account, or a new analytics product.
- Buying a higher plan or changing unrelated Supabase projects.

## What we'll test

- Guest, ordinary user, forged client role/user_metadata, expired token, and trusted admin on both pages and direct API calls.
- Retry double-click/concurrent runs, quota response, job failure/recovery, invalid correction, and import after a correction.
- Manual notice before start, at expiry, with invalid dates/IDs, and clearly different from a source notice.
- Retention deletes only expired eligible history, keeps latest state and required personal records, and stays within free-plan budgets.
- Logs contain no credentials or private trips; an actual documented backup/restore drill and reversible deployment rollback are recorded.

## Resources

- [Supabase row-level security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
- [Supabase production checklist](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod)
- [Supabase Cron](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/cron)
- [Supabase database backups](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups)

title: [Week 3] Production deployment, full-app testing, and ship gate
body:
## Summary

Deploy ArchRide and verify the **whole agreed app** is ready to ship by the November 1 handoff. Closing this task means a working production URL, real authorized transit data, passing checks, and completed user journeys—not a successful build of placeholder screens.

## Background

All tasks 1–11 must be integrated before the release is accepted. The repository’s [CI workflow](https://github.com/nandanpraveen/ArchRide/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml), `docs/APP_BRIEF.md`, and roadmap coverage matrix define the release baseline. Assign a release owner, but the team fixes defects in their own features.

This is a **Week 3** task, from **2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01**, with the Sunday handoff in **America/New_York**. Claim the draft in the project before starting.

## Requirements

- [ ] Deploy a production Next.js build to an agreed suitable host, connect the ArchRide Supabase project, configure server secrets, Auth redirects/site URL, scheduled ingestion/jobs, HTTPS, and any supported push keys. Use no paid upgrades without explicit approval.
- [ ] Complete every requirement from tasks 1–11 and remove visible starter placeholders, fake/live-demo data, dead controls, and unresolved ship-blocking TODOs from production. Every brief feature has an owner and a verified outcome.
- [ ] Run the full guest journey: search building → compare walking/bus → verify boarding direction → start trip → leave-now reminder → recovery/arrival. Run signed-in favorites, schedule, preferences, sign-out, and account deletion on production.
- [ ] Add integration/security coverage with two separate users and anonymous access, direct admin API attacks, all exposed tables/RLS/grants, session refresh, and post-deletion tokens. Confirm no secret key in browser assets, source control, responses, or logs.
- [ ] Test Home, map, route/stop details, Plan, Saved, Profile, alerts, notifications, classes, admin, and active trips on current target desktop/mobile browsers. Include real iPhone/Safari and Android/Chrome smoke tests, keyboard/screen-reader flows, 320 px width, contrast, reduced motion, and safe areas.
- [ ] Exercise denied GPS, outside-campus origin, slow/offline network, source outage/stale data, rate limits, no buses, malformed records, unreachable boarding, unsupported future trips, timezone/DST, expired jobs, denied push, and refresh/reopen recovery.
- [ ] Check real feed freshness and request volume, database growth/retention, walking/map provider quotas/attribution, loading performance, API timeouts, and useful production health monitoring. Record evidence rather than claiming measured accuracy without data.
- [ ] Publish a concise privacy/location notice, student-built affiliation statement, supported-browser/push limitations, README onboarding, operations/rollback runbook, release notes, production URL, and ownership for ongoing operation.
- [ ] Run CI on the final release commit, perform a production smoke test and rollback check, tag the release, and record the acceptance checklist and known non-blocking limitations. Any broken core journey or unapproved data access keeps this task open.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass. Add meaningful feature tests, including the cases below.

## Out of scope

- New features beyond the approved brief, app-store packaging, or promising transit accuracy/notification delivery guarantees.
- Calling a demo complete while a required feature, live-data access, security check, or production deployment is missing.

## What we'll test

- Every feature in the coverage matrix has a reproducible passing acceptance result on the final commit.
- Guest and two-user end-to-end flows including account switching, deletion, private-data isolation, and direct admin access attempts.
- Real device/browser matrix, accessibility, narrow layouts, navigation/deep links, loading and all unavailable states.
- Source failures/recovery, reminders after edits, missed-bus alternatives, loop directions, daylight saving on November 1, and cold production requests.
- Clean-machine setup from README, successful CI, production health/feed checks, rollback, restored operation, and no credentials in Git history or shipped assets.

## Resources

- [Next.js deployment](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/deploying)
- [Supabase production checklist](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod)
- [Playwright testing](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro)
- [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
